chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Ibn Muskan, from Shurahbil al-Kindi, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), he said:

I said: 'How would the menstruating woman know that she has become pure?' He said: 'She should lean her left leg against the wall, and insert the cotton with her right hand. If there was something the like of the head of a fly that came out upon the cotton, (she is still menstruating).'

key_terms.الطَّامِثُ: the menstruating woman (hayd); a woman in the state of ritual impurity due to menstruation
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفَ: cotton (kursuf); a piece of cotton or cloth used to test for the presence of menstrual blood
key_terms.الْيُسْرَى: left (yusra); the left side, used in the prescribed posture for the test
key_terms.الْيُمْنَى: right (yumna); the right side, the hand with which the cotton is to be inserted
key_terms.طُهْرَهَا: her purity (tuhr); the state of ritual cleanliness following the end of menstruation

ai.seo_question: How does a menstruating woman determine that she has become ritually pure according to Imam al-Sadiq in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a practical legal ruling on how a menstruating woman can determine the end of her ritual impurity (hayd). The Imam describes a physical test using cotton: a specific posture (left leg against wall) and insertion with the right hand, after which the presence of even the smallest trace of blood—described hyperbolically as the size of a fly's head—indicates she has not yet achieved ritual purity. This ruling belongs to the chapter on the absolution (itlaq) of the menstruating woman in classical Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Salma Bin Al Khattab, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Tatary, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Ibn Muskan, from Shurahbeyl Al Kindy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said, ‘How would the menstruating woman recognise that she is clean?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would lean with her left leg against the wall, and she would insert the cloth with her right hand. So she was (still) menstruating, (blood) the like of the head of the fly would come out upon the cloth’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Salmah ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Hassan al-Tatariy, from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah, from ibn Muskan, from Shurahbil al-Kindiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about how a woman experiencing Hayd (menses) can find out if her Hayd (menses) has ended. He (the Imam), said, ‘She can find out by leaning against a wall on her left leg and place a piece of cotton in her urethra with her right hand. If there is blood even of the size of fly’s head on the tip of the piece of cotton (it has not ended).”’
